apparatus.basis: definite article on ⲛⲁⲍⲧⲉ 'faith,' standard opening to a virtue-list
ⲣ̄-ⲁⲅⲁⲑⲟⲛ 'do-good' — Greek loan ἀγαθόν; standard ascetic-virtue list pattern
Lycopolitan ⲙ̄ⲙⲁϩ = Sahidic ⲙ̄ⲙⲟϥ 'in it,' anaphoric reference to the prayer
feminine definite article on ⲣⲏⲛⲏ (εἰρήνη) 'peace'; ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲉⲙ ⲛ̄ϯⲣⲏⲛⲏ 'right hand of peace' is standard formula
habitual prefix ϣⲁⲩ- 'they (do habitually)' before ⲱⲕ (= ⲃⲱⲕ 'go')
conjunctive ⲛ̄ⲥⲉ- 'and they' before ⲱⲁⲡⲟⲩ 'receive them'
ⲉ-ⲩ-ⲙⲣ̄ 'while they are bound'; circumstantial preceding parallel ⲉⲩⲭⲁⲗⲭ
ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ 'upward' completed; final ⲓ trace expected
ⲕⲁⲧⲁ 'according to' completed at line break
ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ 'all of them' — completion of expected pronoun
ⲛⲟⲩⲉ̄ = ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲁ 'a one/a man' — completes the comparison
ⲧⲏⲣϩ 'all of it' + ϣⲟⲡ 'is/dwells'; ⲡⲉϩⲕⲟⲙⲓⲧⲁⲧⲟⲛ ⲧⲏⲣϩ ϣⲟⲡ ⲍⲛ̄ 'his entire comitatus dwells in...'
standard collocation: villages of the country (χώρα); fits geographical-administrative inventory cities/dwellings/villages

notes.decision: Rendered 'giving-of-fear' preserving the verbal idiom ϯ + ⲍⲟⲩⲗⲧⲉ ('give fear,' i.e. fear of God). The compound parallels ϯⲣⲉⲛ 'give a name' and similar idioms; the noun ⲍⲟⲩⲗⲧⲉ = ϩⲣⲟⲧⲉ 'fear' (cf. accumulated tentative entry ⲍⲟⲩⲗⲧⲉ).

Translated 'praying' here, paired with ⲛⲏⲥⲧⲓⲁ 'fasting' throughout this kephalaion. While accumulated vocab tentatively suggests ⲡⲉϩⲱⲗⲏⲛ might mean 'his struggle,' the present context (paralleled three times with fasting and once described as 'the prayer that he prayed' — ⲡⲱⲗⲏⲛ ⲉⲧⲁϩⲱⲗⲏⲛ, line 3) decisively fixes it as 'pray/prayer.' This refines the prior tentative reading.
'The releaser' (already in glossary) — agentive of ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'release.' Here functions as the cosmic figure attending the catechumen's first works, conveying their release.

Rendered 'body of light' rather than 'abode of light' or 'ship of light.' The accumulated tentative reading 'the abode' is here refined: the works are received ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ 'inward' into this entity, which is then qualified ⲛⲧⲉ ⲧⲟⲩⲱⲛ 'of the gods.' The cosmic Body of Light (the divine soma into which freed light-particles are gathered) fits Manichaean technical usage. Could also be 'vessel of light.'
Read as 'the gods' (Lycopolitan plural of ⲛⲟⲩⲧⲉ); the genitive ⲛⲧⲉ ⲧⲟⲩⲱⲛ qualifies the body of light as belonging to the divine beings. Alternative: a verbal form 'they open.' Confidence moderate.

ⲭⲁⲗⲭ in glossary = 'mingle, fashion together' — here in the negative-cosmic register: the first works dwell within things 'while bound, while mingled' (i.e. entangled in matter). Pairs with ⲉⲩⲙⲣ̄ 'while bound.'

ⲟⲱ rendered 'stay/remain' (Lyc reflex possibly of ⲱϩⲉ 'stand' or ⲟⲩⲱⲛ 'remain'). With negation ⲉⲛ + ⲍⲓⲃⲁⲗ 'outside' = 'do not stay outside.' The works do not remain external to the catechumen waiting; they are intrinsic to him until bodily death.
ⲥⲁⲙⲧ = qualitative of ⲥⲱⲙⲧ 'look out, watch, await' (Crum). 'Watching for him' fits the imagery: works do not wait outside the man.
= ⲧϭⲟⲙ 'the power' with assimilation. Standard Lycopolitan/scribal contraction.

= 'his comitatus' — Latin comitatus via Greek κομιτᾶτον (already in glossary). In this parable the comitatus is the imperial-style retinue of the man going to a city: it represents the catechumen's works being assembled in advance of his arrival.
